name: deep-chain
summary: A ten-certificate ML-DSA-87 chain: depth stress rather than single-artifact size.
description: Ten ML-DSA-87 certificates from root to leaf, each with a 4,627-byte signature and a 2,592-byte public key. Where jumbo and worst-case-tls stress how big one artifact can be, this stresses how many of them a path builder will walk: ten is exactly the default cap in some TLS stacks, so this fixture sits on the boundary where a chain stops being rejected for its size and starts being rejected for its length. Every CA in the chain carries a pathlen that permits exactly the certificates beneath it, so a verifier that ignores pathlen and one that honours it reach the same answer.
breaks: Path-building algorithms whose cost grows with depth
Verifiers that recurse once per certificate over a fixed stack
Certificate-store APIs that expect a leaf and one intermediate
